To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tumor type M2-pyruvate kinase is increased in colon carcinomas compared to normal colon mucosa from the same patient.
the amount of tumor type M 2-PK in blood sera is a sensitive and specific marker for the presence of colon carcinoma.
the amount of tumor type M 2-PK measured in the serum of healthy blood donors is significantly lower than in the serum of patients suffering from a colon carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of tumor type pyruate kinase (TuM2-PK) by means of ELISA.
the detection of a tumor specific isoenzyme (Tu M2-pyruvate kinase) in serum and tissue of cancer patients.
the quantification of a tumor-specific isoenzyme in blood sera and in tumor tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tumor type M2-pyruvate kinase is increased in colon carcinoma and in serum of patients with colon carcinoma.
the tumor M2-Pk isoenzyme is increased in colon carcinoma tissue, and that it can be measured in the serum.
the tumor type M2-pyruvate kinase is expressed in the tumor and can be quantified both in the serum and in the tissue of patients with colorectal cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tumor type M2-pyruvate kinase in blood serum is a sensitive and specific tumor marker for colon cancer.
the tumor M2-Pk can be measured by ELISA in serum and tumor homogenate of colon carcinoma patients with high specificity and high sensitivity.
we have developed a sensitive and specific ELISA to quantify tumor type M2-pyruvate kinase in serum and in tissue homogenates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of the amount of tumor type M-2-PK in serum can be used as a tumor marker for colon cancer.
tumor type pyruvic kinase can be quantitated in serum and tissue of cancer patients and that this enzyme can be used as a biomarker for cancer detection.
we can use the tumor type M2-pyruvate kinase as a marker for the detection of colon carcinoma.
